```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

This example uses actual USGS National Geochemical Database (NGDB) records from
the project **NAWQA Upper Illinois R. Basin**, selected by its metadata label and
state `IL`, without selecting on silver or other concentrations. It demonstrates
how to retain censored results, examine sampling support and compare descriptive
geometric means across declustering scales.

The saved November 2026 input snapshot contains **439 sample records, 20,422
best-value chemistry records, 48 reported species and 332 numeric geographic
coordinate pairs**. These are different counts. Coordinate matches do not certify
physical sites, replicates, comparable specimens or spatial independence.
Collection dates are absent in this cohort; submission dates are not substituted.
Different versions of the source tables may produce different counts.

This heterogeneous project cohort is a software example, not an established
geological background population. The separate research experiment using 77
Illinois-derived positions has **synthetic responses** and is not the chemistry
analysis shown here. A narrower 142-record support stratum used in exploratory
research is also distinct from the full cohort.

## Obtain and identify the inputs

Obtain the sediment `main.csv` and `bestvalue.csv` exports from the
[USGS NGDB portal](https://mrdata.usgs.gov/ngdb/). Keep the download metadata and
original files unchanged. This example expects the native long-format best-value
table, with `lab_id`, `species`, `unit`, `qvalue` and the available method/summary
columns. It does not treat raw alternative assays as selected best values.
No data download is performed when building this vignette.

The tested snapshot has these SHA256 fingerprints:

| Original sediment export | SHA256 |
| --- | --- |
| `main.csv` | `e67d5bfbebf6ceb9502e9e421948d1711c47537b51414f98a362fa0ad7d8faa9` |
| `bestvalue.csv` | `291591c10a664b5be7fca534bdb746d01aa9306f3280f2e48ad36641cbeff60c` |

Hashes identify a particular file, not its scientific accuracy. Preserve and
report your own source/version if yours differs; do not edit files to match counts.
The package does not bundle the source tables or the project's private research
folder. Start with the offline [synthetic workflow](usgs-workflow.html) if you do
not yet have the data.

## Run the installed example

Install the final geoCensor 1.2.0 release and restart R. An earlier local package
also labeled 1.2.0 can lack the new workflows; the installed commands check the
required capabilities as well as the version. The optional **sf** package is
needed only if this script prepares the projected coordinates itself.

```{r locate-command, eval=FALSE}
library(geoCensor)
script <- system.file("examples", "illinois_case_study.R", package = "geoCensor")
stopifnot(nzchar(script))
system2(file.path(R.home("bin"), "Rscript"),
        shQuote(c(script, "--help")))
```

From a terminal, run the installed script at the path returned above:

```{r run-project, eval=FALSE}
# Run this command from R, using your own local paths and a new output directory.
system2(file.path(R.home("bin"), "Rscript"), shQuote(c(
  script, "ngdbsed/main.csv", "ngdbsed/bestvalue.csv", "illinois_results"
)))
```

The script scans both inputs in batches, reads every field as text, validates
even unselected CSV records and retains all chemistry belonging to the selected
metadata IDs. Input record indices are saved separately from the original
columns. Its default batch size is 10,000; retained data grow with the selected
cohort. It does not infer missing results or silently average repeated assays.

It appends EPSG:5070 metre coordinates by transforming the published
`long_wgs84`/`lat_wgs84` fields, retaining original coordinates, datum and precision
labels. This is a coordinate transformation, not a correction to sample location.
The unresolved location of D346381 remains as recorded. The projection software
and its versions are included in provenance.

Alternatively, provide previously prepared EPSG:5070 coordinates with one
`lab_id`, `x_m`, `y_m` row per selected sample. Their CRS/units are your explicit
assertion; numeric columns alone cannot establish a CRS:

```{r supplied-projection, eval=FALSE}
system2(file.path(R.home("bin"), "Rscript"), shQuote(c(
  script, "ngdbsed/main.csv", "ngdbsed/bestvalue.csv", "illinois_repeat",
  "--projected-metadata=reviewed_metadata_projected.csv"
)))
```

The output directory must not exist and its parent must exist. Another run uses
a new name. Partial outputs from a write failure are retained for review.

## Audit before interpreting an estimate

```{r review-results, eval=FALSE}
results <- readRDS("illinois_results/analysis.rds")
support <- readRDS("illinois_results/support.rds")
provenance <- readRDS("illinois_results/provenance.rds")
read.csv("illinois_results/inventory.csv")
support$fields
support$coordinate_groups
results$estimates[c("element", "state", "n_total", "n_exact", "n_left",
                    "n_right", "geomean", "review_status")]
results$methods
```

Read the support and method tables with the chemistry results. Uncensored coding
does not certify analytical precision, and an unreviewed method is not a cleared
method. Missing metadata remain unknown. Reported support descriptions vary;
pooling the project for this demonstration is not evidence of a common analyzed
fraction or geological population.

All 48 species remain visible, including four carbon-related labels. In the tested
snapshot, **Au, Bi, Eu, Ho and Ta are all left-censored and their geometric means
are unavailable**. They remain in the tables rather than disappearing from a
chart. No concentration is assigned to an absent species, and no zero or fraction
of a limit replaces a nondetect.

## Examine Ag and the other reported species

```{r silver-sensitivity, eval=FALSE}
ag <- subset(results$declustering, element == "Ag")
ag[c("cell_size", "n_total", "n_left", "unweighted_geomean", "geomean",
     "weighted_exact_fraction", "weight_effective_n", "ci_low", "ci_high")]
results$source_precision_summary
```

The same selected cohort can be analyzed directly through the API. Keep original
metadata text separate from its explicit numeric-coordinate analysis copy:

```{r direct-api, eval=FALSE}
chemistry <- read_usgs_chemistry("illinois_results/selected_chemistry.csv")
metadata <- readr::read_csv("illinois_results/metadata_projected.csv",
  col_types = readr::cols(.default = readr::col_character()),
  trim_ws = FALSE, show_col_types = FALSE)
for (name in c("x_m", "y_m")) {
  value <- readr::parse_double(metadata[[name]])
  stopifnot(nrow(readr::problems(value)) == 0L)
  metadata[[name]] <- value
}
spatial <- analyze_elements(
  chemistry, main_df = metadata, group_cols = "state",
  cell_sizes = c(5000, 10000, 20000), x_col = "x_m", y_col = "y_m",
  n_offsets = 10, stratify_methods = TRUE,
  audit_method_overlap = TRUE, audit_source_precision = TRUE
)
stopifnot(identical(spatial, results))
```

Cell widths of 5, 10 and 20 km are fixed sensitivity choices, not an optimized
geological scale. Ten offsets per axis give 100 grid placements. Weighted and
unweighted fits use the same usable chemistry/coordinate subset. Declustering
changes descriptive influence; its weight effective sample size is not a count
of independent observations. Estimates are in **ug/kg**, while original source
values and source-summary precision differences retain their original units.

The script creates `recorded_positions.png` and `declustering_sensitivity.png`.
The latter compares Ag, Pb, Zn, Cu and Hg for readability; the CSV/RDS outputs
retain every reported species and unavailable result. Source-precision candidates
are review evidence and never replace the estimation inputs.

`Ag_cdf_bounds.csv` and its plot show the range of possible empirical cumulative
fractions given the recorded Ag values and limits, using equal record weights.
These reporting-information bounds use all usable Ag records, including records
without coordinates. They are not spatial confidence bands, a fitted distribution
or a declustering adjustment. No values are imputed within the recorded ranges.

## What this example establishes

The example demonstrates traceable selection, preserved reporting bounds,
sampling-support review and descriptive sensitivity to clustering. It does not
identify concentrations on unsampled land, validate anomalies or ore probability,
or distinguish geological enrichment from human contamination or analytical error.
Unknown collection dates, historical exposure and dilution remain unknown.

Ordinary model intervals retain their independence/lognormal assumptions.
**Weighted routine confidence limits remain absent; spatial confidence limits
remain experimental.** Numerical convergence and a successful software test are
not evidence of calibrated coverage. Further covariance-refitting, censoring and
model-misspecification experiments are needed before promoting spatial inference.

The output includes original selected metadata, projected analysis metadata,
chemistry, source-record indices, support/results tables, MD5 input/output
fingerprints, configuration and session information. These support reproducibility;
they do not certify source accuracy or missing QA. Keep the source exports and
run directory with any report derived from the example.
